4:105:10.noteEnglish: QAC tags أَرَىٰكَ a 1st-person singular subjunctive imperfect, but in بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ the nominative ٱللَّهُ is its subject and no particle of nasb precedes it: it is the Form IV perfect أَرَى (He showed you), 3rd masculine singular, in the relative clause of مَا. The generated i'rab line 'مضارع منصوب' follows the faulty tag.

4:108:14.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَرْضَىٰ subjunctive, but in مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ the لَا is plain negation inside a relative clause and nothing governs nasb; it is indicative with an implied damma on the alif maqsura.

4:124:15.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُظْلَمُونَ jussive, but its nun is retained (sign of raf') after negative لَا; it is joined to the nominal answer فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ, which is not in jazm, so it is indicative.

4:127:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُتْلَىٰ subjunctive, but in وَمَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ the مَا is relative and no particle of nasb precedes; it is an indicative passive with an implied damma on the alif maqsura.

4:140:11.noteEnglish: QAC omits PASS, but يُكْفَرُ has prefix-u with fatha on the fa (active Form I would be يَكْفُرُ): it is the Form I passive (they are disbelieved in), with بِهَا as na'ib al-fa'il, parallel to the passive وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا.

rejected.reason: كُنَّا is the active Form I perfect of the hollow verb كَانَ (kunnā); the u is the hollow-verb vowel, not a passive marker.
كُنتَ is the active perfect of hollow كَانَ; the damma comes from the weak root, not the passive.
كُنتُم is the active perfect of hollow كَانَ; the damma comes from the weak root, not the passive.
فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ is the answer of the conditional after فَ + سَوْفَ, so it is not in jazm; the ya is kept with an implied damma (indicative).
وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ is joined to indicative يَعِدُهُمْ with no governing particle; the final ya is kept with an implied damma, so indicative is correct.
جَنَّـٰتٍ is a sound feminine plural, so its accusative takes kasra; it is the second object of سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ (i'rab: منصوب).
تَجْرِى describes جَنَّـٰتٍ with no governing particle; indicative with implied damma on the ya.
يُجْزَ is the jussive answer of مَن يَعْمَلْ; its final alif is dropped for jazm, leaving fatha (i'rab: مجزوم).
ٱللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ is the predicate of a nominal sentence with no governing particle; indicative with implied damma on the ya.
تَلْوُۥٓا۟ is the jussive verb of the conditional وَإِن; the five-verbs nun is dropped for jazm (i'rab: مجزوم).
سَوْفَ يُؤْتِيهِمْ has no governing particle (سَوْفَ does not cause jazm); indicative with implied damma on the ya.
وَقُلْنَا is the active perfect of hollow قَالَ (We said), with نَا as subject; the damma comes from the weak root.
وَقُلْنَا is the active perfect of hollow قَالَ (We said), with نَا as subject; the damma comes from the weak root.
طَيِّبَـٰتٍ is a sound feminine plural, so its accusative takes kasra; it is the object of حَرَّمْنَا.
سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ is the predicate of أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ after future سَ with no governing particle; indicative with implied damma on the ya.
فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ follows the فَ answering أَمَّا, which does not cause jazm; the ya is kept with an implied damma (indicative).
